title: Touring with Bill Davis and running his own booking office
summary: He manages Bill Davis in California for a hundred dollars and expenses and back home runs his own saxophone-studio booking office.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So when another guy quit at Shaw, he came... I had gone to California with Bill Davis. Because I worked out a deal with him. I was only making about fifty dollars commission. So I worked out a deal with him if he could give me another fifty dollars, making my salary a hundred dollars and my expenses, I would go on the road with him, be out there as personal manager with him on the road. Because he had the records going and everything. So we did. So I went out to California with him.

And when I came back to the office... In my office, I had a set-up where I had a girl taking care of one thing, a sister who was taking care of the booking, the bookkeeping. And they were doing something I didn't like about the business. Because they brought some guy in that we didn't need. I was doing all the booking. We didn't need him. He was probably smoking marijuana and all that...
Were you still getting your commissions from the booking agency while you were out there?
All the things I'd booked for them went out, yes. So Shaw called me over, and he wanted to offer me a job! And I was doing good enough, although I wasn't doing as good as I could, but I was...
Who were you working for now?
I was working for nobody now. But I was working for myself. And he called me up, and he said...
I mean, who did you have in your office who was booking. You said...
Well, I had Esther Lauro(?). She was...
That was your own booking office.
Yeah, my... See, that's when I had my saxophone studio, and I started booking out of there. That's where I started my personal management.
I know that girl Esther. She was ...(?)...
